title: Set 154

sentences.ko: 설탕 끊고 진짜 잘 버티고 있었는데, 월요일에 회사 동료가 도넛을 사 와서 하나쯤은 괜찮겠지 했거든. 근데 하나가 세 개가 되더니, 수요일쯤엔 거의 다시 먹고 싶은 거 다 먹고 있더라.
sentences.text: I was doing so well with no sugar, and then my coworker brought in donuts on Monday and I figured one wouldn't hurt. But one turned into three, and by Wednesday I was basically eating whatever I wanted again.

alts.text: No sugar was going great till my coworker showed up with donuts Monday, and I figured one's fine, right? One turned into three, and by Wednesday I was pretty much eating whatever again.

I had been doing very well without sugar, but then a colleague brought donuts to the office on Monday, and I assumed that one would not do any harm. However, one became three, and by Wednesday I was essentially eating whatever I wanted once again.

sentences.note: **one wouldn't hurt** 는 하나쯤은 괜찮겠지라는 뜻으로, 자기 합리화할 때 자주 씁니다. **turned into** 는 어느새 ~가 되어 버렸다는 느낌입니다.

sentences.ko: 안녕하세요, 위층 사는 사람인데 또 연락드려요. 난방이 아직도 안 돼요. 지난주에 누가 와 본다고 하셨는데 결국 아무도 안 왔어요. 밤에 점점 너무 추워져서 그러는데, 그냥 수리 기사님 번호 주시면 제가 직접 전화할게요.
sentences.text: Hi, it's me from upstairs again. The heat still isn't working, and I know you said someone would come by last week, but nobody ever showed up. It's getting really cold at night, so could you just give me the guy's number and I'll call him myself?

alts.text: Hey, upstairs again. Heat's still out. You said somebody'd come by last week, but nobody ever showed. It gets super cold at night, so can I just get the guy's number and call him myself?

Hello, this is your tenant from upstairs again. The heating is still not working, and I understand you said someone would come by last week, but no one ever arrived. It is becoming very cold at night, so would you please give me the technician's number so that I may call him myself?

sentences.note: **come by** 는 잠깐 들르다라는 뜻입니다. **showed up** 은 약속한 사람이 나타나다, 오다라는 뜻으로 nobody ever showed up 은 결국 아무도 안 왔다입니다.
sentences.situation: 집주인이랑 고장 난 것 고쳐 달라고 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 나 혼자 정하는 거면 차 빌려줄 텐데, 그 주에 아내가 출근할 때 차를 써야 해. 지금 된다고 해 놓고 막판에 가서 못 빌려준다고 하고 싶진 않아서.
sentences.text: I'd lend you the car if it were just up to me, but my wife needs it for work that week, and I don't want to say yes now and then have to back out at the last minute.

alts.text: If it was just my call, the car's yours, but my wife's gotta have it for work that week. Don't wanna say yes now and then bail last minute.
I would lend you the car if the decision were mine alone, but my wife requires it for work that week, and I would not want to agree now and then have to withdraw at the last minute.

sentences.note: **up to me** 는 내가 정할 일이다라는 뜻입니다. **back out** 은 하기로 한 약속을 물리다, 발을 빼다라는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 네가 맨날 얘기하던 그 라멘집 드디어 가 봤는데, 솔직히 왜 다들 난리인지 모르겠어. 국물이 너무 짜서 밤새 목말랐어. 내가 메뉴를 잘못 시켰나?
sentences.text: So I finally tried that ramen place you keep talking about, and honestly, I don't get the hype. The broth was really salty, and I was thirsty the whole night. Maybe I just ordered the wrong thing?

alts.text: Tried your ramen place. Honestly? Don't get the hype. Super salty broth, I was thirsty all night. Maybe I ordered wrong?

I finally visited the ramen restaurant you have mentioned so often, and to be honest, I do not understand the enthusiasm. The broth was very salty, and I was thirsty for the entire evening. Perhaps I simply ordered the wrong dish?

sentences.note: **I don't get the hype** 는 다들 좋다고 하는데 나는 왜 그런지 모르겠다는 뜻입니다. **you keep talking about** 은 네가 계속 얘기하는이라는 뜻으로 살짝 놀리는 느낌이 있습니다.
sentences.situation: 친구가 추천한 식당 다녀와서 후기 말하기

sentences.ko: 1월에 기타를 샀거든. 예전부터 늘 배워 보고 싶었거든. 한 달 정도는 매일 밤 연습했어. 근데 손가락이 아프기 시작하고 일도 바빠져서, 지금은 그냥 침실 벽에 기대 세워져 있어. 왠지 나를 한심하게 쳐다보는 것 같아.
sentences.text: I bought a guitar back in January because I'd always wanted to learn, and I practiced every night for like a month. But then my fingers started hurting and work got busy, so now it's just leaning against the wall in the bedroom, kind of judging me.

alts.text: Bought a guitar in January, played every night for like a month. Then my fingers hurt, work got crazy, and now it's just sitting in the bedroom, kinda judging me.

I purchased a guitar in January because I had always wanted to learn, and I practiced every evening for about a month. However, my fingers began to hurt and work became busy, so it is now simply leaning against the bedroom wall, almost as though it is judging me.

sentences.note: **leaning against** 는 ~에 기대어 있다는 뜻입니다. **kind of judging me** 는 물건이 나를 탓하는 것 같다는 농담으로, kind of 가 말을 부드럽게 해 줍니다.

reviewed: 5번 casual 이 text 와 앞부분이 거의 같아서(Got a guitar back in January cause I'd always wanted to learn...) 더 짧고 축약된 구어로 새로 씀
5번 한국어 '원래부터 늘 배워 보고 싶었어서' 가 어색해서 '예전부터 늘 배워 보고 싶었거든' 으로 고침
4번 casual 이 text 와 같은 순서로 같은 말을 이어 가서 더 짧게 끊은 구어로 바꿈
